title: SightBench: does the parcel match?

headlines.label: Mismatches flagged on the frozen test split, Sightline
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. Stratified over colour, size, model and damage mismatches. CLIP's dev-fitted threshold also flags 189 of 210 (90.0%) of matching pairs (dev balanced accuracy 0.5444), so its recall says little.

headlines.label: Matching items wrongly called a mismatch (false alarms), Sightline
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. A false alarm tells a buyer to return an item that is right. 1 of 4 came from a "sure" colour disagreement (listed: rust, burgundy, navy, sky blue); see details.worstCases.sightlineFalseAlarms.

headlines.label: Pairs where Sightline answered "not sure" (abstained)
headlines.note: Coverage 137 of 420 (32.6%). Accuracy when Sightline did answer: 132 of 137 (96.4%); CLIP accuracy: 215 of 420 (51.2%).

headlines.label: Accuracy when Sightline gives an answer (match or mismatch)
Secondary metric, added after the first test run: mismatches where Sightline names the difference (mismatch, or "not sure" with the right module disagreeing)
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. What the buyer hears, for example "The size tag seems to read L, you ordered M, but I'm only fairly sure.", and the money-back path stays open for "not sure". Per type: colour 14 of 53, damage 47 of 52, model 43 of 52, size 44 of 53. Defined after the first test run's primary numbers were known, so it is reported next to them, never instead of them.

headlines.label: False-alarm twin of the secondary metric: matching items called a mismatch or given any disagreeing reason
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. The buyer hears a difference that is not there, even if only as "not sure". Disagreeing modules on these pairs: damage 87, colour 21, identity 3.

headlines.label: First test run (unfitted thresholds, 2026-11-08): mismatches flagged / false alarms / not sure
headlines.note: The frozen test split has been run 4 times: first with the hand-set thresholds, then with thresholds fitted on the dev split only. Nothing was tuned on test. Every run's numbers are in details.testRuns. Mismatches flagged per type, first run -> this run: colour 4 -> 2 of 53, damage 2 -> 32 of 52, model 0 -> 43 of 52, size 1 -> 44 of 53. Secondary metric, first run -> this run: named 76 of 210 -> 148 of 210, twin false alarms 45 of 210 -> 100 of 210.

headlines.label: Navy delivered for black (or black for navy) in dim light: mismatches caught by Sightline
headlines.baseline: in daylight: 0 of 7; CLIP dim: 7 of 7
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. In dim light the colour module disagreed on 0, but dim light lowers its confidence below "sure", so the verdict was "not sure"; it agreed (wrongly) on 0 and gave up on 7. CLIP's 7 of 7 means little: it flags 90.0% of matching pairs too. Only 7 pairs per light level, so intervals are wide.

headlines.label: Wrong size delivered: caught by Sightline
headlines.note: Size needs both tag reads (model and OCR) to agree before a mismatch is "sure".

headlines.label: Different model or damage marks: caught by Sightline
headlines.note: Identity and damage come from the vision-model reads.

headlines.label: Colour check gave up ("heavy colour cast") on wood tables and plank floors
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. Without a sheet of white paper in view, white balance is gray world over the background, so an orange wood surface reads as a strong colour cast and the colour module abstains. Holds in daylight too. Checked on dev: the item masks on wood are tight and the background pixels are plain wood, so this is the gray-world assumption, not a mask bug; it was not fitted away.

headlines.label: POST /verify latency on the dev laptop, p50 / p95
headlines.note: Client wall time, one request at a time over localhost, CPU only, including model calls. Server-side total p50 6100 ms.

limitations: Synthetic renders, not real photos: listing images are clean procedural renders and delivered photos are phone-like renders (perspective, rotation, uneven light, colour casts, blur, noise, JPEG). Real photos will differ; the real photo set (evals/sightbench/real/SHOTLIST.md) is not collected yet.
This run used the vision-model reads (GET /health vlm.configured true).

Service thresholds: fitted-dev-2026-11-09, fitted on the dev split only (services/vision/app/thresholds.json, "fitted"); the hand-set set is kept as initial-unfitted. The CLIP threshold was also fitted on dev only: 0.880224 (maximise balanced accuracy on dev over midpoints of sorted dev scores; ties -> median tied candidate). Dev has only 180 pairs (23 colour mismatches), so the fit is coarse.

The frozen test split has been run 4 times: run 1 on 2026-11-08 (no-model, unfitted thresholds); run 2 on 2026-11-08 (no-model, thresholds fitted on dev (fitted-dev-2026-11-09)); run 3 on 2026-11-09 (no-model, thresholds fitted on dev (fitted-dev-2026-11-09)); run 4 on 2026-11-09 (with-model, thresholds fitted on dev (fitted-dev-2026-11-09)). Each run's numbers are in details.testRuns; nothing was tuned on test.
The secondary metric ("names the difference" and its false-alarm twin) was defined after the first test run had been scored. It is reported next to the primary metrics, never instead of them.
The test split (420 pairs, sha256 e7561f6ddae5) was frozen before any system ran. Products never cross splits (check-splits.mjs).
One delivered photo, one tag photo (not for mugs) and one listing image per pair; no damage close-up was sent, because a blind buyer may not know where to aim.
Navy/black is deliberately oversampled (40% of colour mismatches), but that is still 7 pairs per light level; per-cell intervals are wide.
The CLIP baseline sees only the listing image and the delivered photo, never the tag or the listing text, so it cannot see size by design.
Ablations are decision rules applied to the module outputs of the same /verify calls, not separate service runs.

details.label: Synthetic renders, not real photos. With vision-model reads.

dev.usedFor: fitting the CLIP threshold and the service thresholds (colour confidence rules)

fitted.decision: mismatch when cosine(listing image, delivered photo) < threshold, else match; never abstains
fitted.rule: maximise balanced accuracy on dev over midpoints of sorted dev scores; ties -> median tied candidate

clip.label: CLIP ViT-B/32 image similarity
clip.definition: cosine(listing image, delivered photo) < 0.880224 -> mismatch, else match. Threshold fitted on dev only (maximise balanced accuracy on dev over midpoints of sorted dev scores; ties -> median tied candidate).

colourOnly.label: Colour module only (any confidence)
colourOnly.definition: modules.colour.finding: disagree -> mismatch, agree -> match, unknown -> unsure.

colourStrict.label: Colour module only (fusion confidence rule)
colourStrict.definition: disagree at "sure" -> mismatch; agree at "fairly sure" or better -> match; else unsure.

ocrOnly.label: Size-tag OCR only
ocrOnly.definition: modules.size.read_b (OCR) compared with the listing size: different -> mismatch, same -> match; no read, no size or not comparable -> unsure.

ranking.rule: Sorted by the lower end of the 95% bootstrap interval of F1 (mismatch = positive, "unsure" = not flagged); ties by the Wilson lower bound of mismatch recall.
ranking.caveat: With 50% mismatches, flagging every pair scores F1 = 2/3 (the reference row). Read F1 together with recallMinusFalseAlarm (0 for flagging everything) and coverage.

table.label: Reference only: flag every pair as a mismatch

clip.label: CLIP ViT-B/32 image similarity
clip.definition: cosine(listing image, delivered photo) < 0.880224 -> mismatch, else match. Threshold fitted on dev only (maximise balanced accuracy on dev over midpoints of sorted dev scores; ties -> median tied candidate).

colourOnly.label: Colour module only (any confidence)
colourOnly.definition: modules.colour.finding: disagree -> mismatch, agree -> match, unknown -> unsure.

colourStrict.label: Colour module only (fusion confidence rule)
colourStrict.definition: disagree at "sure" -> mismatch; agree at "fairly sure" or better -> match; else unsure.

ocrOnly.label: Size-tag OCR only
ocrOnly.definition: modules.size.read_b (OCR) compared with the listing size: different -> mismatch, same -> match; no read, no size or not comparable -> unsure.

definition.namesTheDifference: A mismatching pair whose verdict is mismatch, or unsure with a disagreeing reason from the module matching the true mismatch type (colour -> colour, size -> size, model -> identity, damage -> damage).
definition.falseAlarmTwin: A matching pair whose verdict is mismatch, or that got any disagreeing reason (the buyer hears a difference that is not there).
definition.added: Added after the first test run, which had already been scored on the primary metrics. Reported next to them, never instead of them.
